post_title: How many viewers (millions, combined average across channels) will Spain's 26 November 2026 televised leaders' debate draw?

question.title: How many viewers (millions, combined average across channels) will Spain's 26 November 2026 televised leaders' debate draw?
question.description:
Spain holds general elections on Sunday 29 November 2026, with the official campaign running from 13 to 27 November. Televised debates are the campaign's highest-profile events, and the final-stretch multi-candidate debate is traditionally the most-watched.

**State of the debate calendar as of 13 November 2026.** After PSOE and PP agreed on 9–10 November that the Academia de Televisión would produce the election debates, the Academia confirmed on 13 November that the Sánchez–Feijóo 'cara a cara' will take place on Thursday 19 November in its Plató A in Madrid, moderated by Academia president María Casado (https://www.academiatv.es/la-academia-de-television-punto-de-encuentro-para-los-debates-electorales-2026). A second, multi-candidate debate ('debate a cuatro', which Podemos is also pressing to join) is likewise to be produced by the Academia; the PP has pushed for Thursday 26 November, three days before the vote, and RTVE's original proposal also included a four-way on 26 November, but the Academia's 13 November note confirmed only the cara a cara date, so the second debate's date, line-up and channel carriage are not yet formally fixed (https://www.elmundo.es/elecciones/elecciones-generales/2026/11/13/6af726a8e4d4d8e5638b4587.html). Other events in the same window: an Atresmedia four-way with Feijóo, Abascal and Colau moved to Monday 23 November, an RTVE debate of seven/eight parliamentary spokespeople on 23 November, and laSexta 'Mesa Abierta' spokesperson panels on 19 and 26 November. Historically the Academia produces an institutional signal that all interested broadcasters may carry live, which is why Spanish debate audiences are reported as a combined figure across channels.

**How the audience is measured.** Viewing data come from Kantar Media's panel; Barlovento Comunicación publishes daily Spanish audience reports ('Audiencias DD de mes AAAA') early each morning, with average audience ('audiencia media') and share per programme and channel, plus dedicated analyses for major debates. Vertele/eldiario, FormulaTV and the main newspapers report the same Kantar-based figures.

**Historical benchmark audiences for election debates** (combined average audience across all channels carrying the debate, Kantar/Barlovento): 7 Dec 2015 four-way 9,233,000 (48.2% share); 14 Dec 2015 Sánchez–Rajoy 9,728,000 (48.7%); 13 Jun 2016 four-way 10,496,000 (57.0%); 22 Apr 2019 RTVE four-way 8,886,000 (43.8%); 23 Apr 2019 Atresmedia four-way 9,477,000 (48.7%); 4 Nov 2019 five-way 8,632,000 (52.7%, carried by 12 channels, 17.3 million cumulative viewers); 10 Jul 2023 Sánchez–Feijóo cara a cara 5,911,000 (46.5%; Antena 3 3,194,000 + laSexta 2,716,000). The 19 Jul 2023 RTVE three-way drew about 4 million. Older debates were larger still (2008 and 2011 cara a cara debates: 12–13 million) (https://barloventocomunicacion.es/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Analisis-Audiencia-Debate-Sanchez-Feijo_10-julio-2023.pdf, https://www.reasonwhy.es/media/library/informe-audiencia-tv-debate-electoral-4n-2019.pdf).

**Current television landscape (November 2026).** Linear TV audiences are well below the levels of 2015–2019: on 12 November 2026 the most-watched programme of the day was the Czech Republic–Spain Nations League match on La 1 with 4,139,000 average viewers and a 30.9% share (peak 5,260,000), while the leading daily news bulletins draw around 2.1–2.3 million; total TV viewing that day was 28.07 million people, 170 minutes per person (https://barloventocomunicacion.es/audiencias-diarias/audiencias-12-de-noviembre-2026/). El País reported on 12 November that a Feijóo interview drew a 12.8% share and 1,725,000 viewers, and noted that serious political debates were still to come in the campaign.

**Political context bearing on interest.** The campaign is dominated by the 28 October Urda rail crash (69 dead) and the resignation of transport minister Óscar Puente, plus an 11 November general strike and the fight over the housing decree — conditions that historically raise political television audiences. The 19 November cara a cara's audience, published on 20 November, will be the closest available calibration point before the 26 November debate.

question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves on the combined average audience ('audiencia media', in millions of viewers) that the televised leaders' debate broadcast on Spanish linear television on 26 November 2026 drew across all channels that aired it. A qualifying debate is one in which candidates for the Presidency of the Government ('cabezas de lista' to Congress) of at least two of the following take part: PSOE (Pedro Sánchez), PP (Alberto Núñez Feijóo), Vox (Santiago Abascal), and the main national left-of-PSOE formation (reported during this campaign as Frente Amplio, with Ada Colau among its leaders); a debate counts whether or not any particular leader attends, and a panel of spokespeople or representatives who are not those candidates does not qualify.

The figure of record is the combined debate audience published by Barlovento Comunicación in its audience publications for 26 November 2026 (https://barloventocomunicacion.es/publicaciones), whether as a dedicated debate analysis or as a combined figure in its daily report for that date. Only if Barlovento publishes no combined figure is the value obtained by adding the debate's per-channel 'audiencia media' listings in that report, counting only channels that aired the debate in full (highlights, excerpts, news items, and delayed or partial broadcasts excluded). The value is expressed in millions of viewers: a debate averaging 5,432,000 viewers across all channels resolves as 5.432.

If no qualifying debate is broadcast on 26 November 2026, the question is annulled; if more than one qualifying debate airs that day, the one with the largest combined average audience is used. If Barlovento publishes no debate figure at all, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) will be used.
question.fine_print: The audience counted is that of the debate broadcast itself, not of any surrounding preview, analysis or post-debate programme; where the source distinguishes the debate segment from a longer programme block, the debate-only figure is used. Peak-minute ('minuto de oro') and cumulative-reach ('espectadores únicos') figures are not used. A debate that begins on 26 November 2026 local time counts even if it runs past midnight.
